worked_example.problem: When an egg is boiled, the clear liquid inside turns white and solid. Is this a physical or a chemical change?
steps: The clear liquid becomes a white solid that does not turn back when it cools.
A new substance has formed and the change cannot be reversed.

cards.idea: A physical change makes no new substance and is often easy to reverse.
example: Ice → water → ice again: the same substance all the time.

cards.idea: A chemical change makes a new substance and is hard to reverse.
example: Firewood burns to ash and smoke: you cannot turn the ash back into wood.

cards.idea: Signs of a chemical change: gas given off, colour change, heat or light given out, a new solid or a new smell.
example: A piece of chalk in vinegar fizzes: a gas is made.

questions.prompt: Water boils and gives bubbles. Why is boiling a physical change?

right.text: The bubbles are steam, which is still water: no new substance is made.

wrong.explain: Many chemical changes also need heat. What matters is whether a new substance forms.

wrong.text: Because bubbles always mean a physical change.
wrong.explain: Bubbles can come from chemical changes too (chalk in vinegar).
The state does not decide; ask whether a new substance forms.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Dissolving sugar is a physical change.
Melting ice can be reversed by freezing.

wrong.text: Cooking an egg is a physical change.
wrong.explain: Cooking makes new substances that do not change back: a chemical change.

wrong.text: Grinding maize into flour is a chemical change.
wrong.explain: Flour is still maize in small pieces: a physical change.
